Q1: Britain. A red-white-blue Union Jack-style flag flies on the tower and walls after 4 Aug 1704, under the caption "1704 — The Rock changes hands". Residents also walk away from the town (frames 26-29).
Q2: The Great Siege. The caption "1779 — The Great Siege" appears, then wooden lines and forts are built across the sand and ships gather offshore.
Q3: They look cut off by a blockade. Ships ring the bay and siege lines wall off the land side. In Jan 1780 a man and woman pick plants on a hillside, which suggests there is little food.
Q4: A fleet of ships arrives at the harbour (frame 59, 12 Apr 1781). I am not sure it is shown as a rescue, but it follows the hunger scenes.
Q5: A big attack at sea on 13-14 Sep 1782. A row of ships sails in at the town, and at night the line of vessels burns and smokes below the Rock. It looks like the attacking ships are destroyed.
Q6: Over the centuries the sand is first covered in siege lines and forts, then empty fields. A first small neighbourhood and a runway appear around 1939, with an airfield by 1942-43. A large dense town of streets and apartment blocks fills the land by 2026.
Q7: Not sure. In Jun-Aug 1969 a dark line or fence shows across the flat land, and nothing is clearly happening at a gate. Nothing in the pictures shows what happens later.
Q8: An airport runway with a crosswalk. Travellers with suitcases walk across it, and in 2026 street scenes and aerials show the two towns side by side on either side of it.

A 1782 flash-forward appears before the 1704 story, so it is unclear why.

A dark night frame with a tiny wall; it is unclear what is happening.

Burning streets at night in Apr 1781, with no clear cause or link to the hunger scenes.
A string of year-only dates over empty fields, with no clue about the point.

Rooftops of a town in 2026 with no label saying which town or why it matters.
